events.pt: Declaração de Independência dos Estados Unidos

narratives: Brazil has been organised around exporting commodities since 1500, and the identity of the buyer kept changing — Portugal, then Britain, then the United States, now China. Each change was political. The walk follows four movements: sugar and gold for the crown that owned the coast; coffee and rubber under terms Britain wrote in 1810 and enforced in 1845; steel, oil and wartime latex traded to the United States for industrial capital, ending in a coup and twenty-one years of dictatorship; and iron ore, soya and oil sold to China since 2009. It is one account among the possible ones. The weight it puts on the buyer is exactly what a second narrative would argue with, and the disputed link at its centre — whether the United States moved against Goulart because of what Brazil produced or out of Cold War anti-communism — is where that argument is sharpest.
